default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-059.title: OBV leads the price high
E-059.hypothesis: When session on-balance volume makes a new high for the window while price is still below its window high, volume on up bars is outpacing volume on down bars before the price has moved (patient accumulation); the sellers capping the price are being worked through, so price follows the volume line (mirror for lows).

E-060.title: Low-volume pullback resumption
E-060.hypothesis: In a session trend (price on the rising side of a rising VWAP), a pullback of several bars each on below-normal volume for its minute shows no real supply, only profit-taking (a Wyckoff 'test'); the first close above the previous bar's high is the trend holders resuming, so follow it (mirror in a down trend).

E-061.title: Session-range traverse follow
E-061.hypothesis: Crossing from the bottom to the top part of the day's developed range within a short time is initiative activity by a longer-timeframe participant, not responsive rotation; such a participant keeps working the order, so the traverse continues past the far edge; follow it (mirror for a fast fall).

E-062.title: Rising-volume run follow
E-062.hypothesis: Consecutive higher closes each traded on more volume than the bar before show participation building into the move: more and more traders are paying up rather than a single burst; flow that keeps growing is a parent order being scaled up, so follow the bar that completes the run when its volume is at least normal.

E-063.title: Impulse-bar midpoint hold
E-063.hypothesis: A large near-full-body bar is a burst of one-sided market orders; its midpoint is the average fill of that burst. The first return to the midpoint that closes back on the impulse side shows the impulse side defending its average price while the counter-traders who faded it are trapped; follow the impulse.

E-064.title: Hikkake inside-bar fakeout
E-064.hypothesis: After an inside bar, a break of only one side of it draws breakout traders in that direction; if price then closes beyond the OTHER side of the inside bar within a few bars, those traders are trapped with stops just behind and the release of the compression goes the other way; follow the fakeout reversal.

E-065.title: Open-at-extreme bar follow
E-065.hypothesis: A bar of at least typical range whose open is its low (no trade below the opening price for the whole bar) and that closes in its upper half shows buyers lifting offers from the first tick with no seller able to push below; demand that strong at the bar's start is a parent order still running, so follow it (mirror).

E-066.title: TD setup count exhaustion fade
E-066.hypothesis: DeMark's TD setup (N consecutive closes above the close four bars earlier) is plotted by many platforms and marks a move carried by late chasers; when the count completes, the trend followers are fully in and counters on many screens flag exhaustion at the same bar, so fade it (mirror for a down count).

E-067.title: Stochastic pop with the VWAP side
E-067.hypothesis: Bernstein-style 'stochastic pop': the fast stochastic reaching overbought is strength, not exhaustion, when price is on the buying side of the session VWAP; short-horizon momentum traders enter there and the oscillator faders' stops sit just above, so follow the pop (mirror for oversold below VWAP).

E-068.title: Up-on-light, down-on-heavy volume asymmetry fade
E-068.hypothesis: When price has risen over the window but the average down bar trades much more volume than the average up bar, the rise is drifting on thin buying while sellers distribute size on every dip; once the asymmetry becomes large the distributing side controls the price, so fade the rise (mirror for a fall).
